content.jointProblem: Can an unsupervised, drift-aware anomaly detection pipeline learn site-specific normal behaviour from unlabelled Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic and raise explainable alerts that stay usable when a site's operating behaviour changes? The collaboration would test this by adapting Vojnović's log and stream anomaly methods to ArmaturaSec's traffic archives and measuring false-positive behaviour against expert-reviewed normal periods and any controlled injections.

rationale.text: Vojnović has a research grounding in unsupervised clustering for distributed system log analysis, directly relevant to learning normal behaviour without attack labels.

sources.quote: dissertation on unsupervised clustering methods for distributed system log analysis

rationale.text: Her work includes adaptive thresholding under non-stationary distributions, which addresses the site-specific baseline drift ArmaturaSec needs.

sources.quote: threshold adaptation scheme based on extreme value theory (EVT)

rationale.text: She has evaluated methods on industrial SCADA and PLC logs from water, heating and food-processing facilities, indicating familiarity with OT data quirks.

sources.quote: logs collected from two SCADA systems in a regional water treatment facility and a district heating network
PLC diagnostic logs recording motor current deviations, sensor timeouts, and safety interlock triggers

rationale.text: She has benchmarked stream processing engines for real-time log anomaly detection, relevant to the latency and throughput constraints of on-device deployment.

sources.quote: compares Apache Flink, Apache Storm, and a custom lightweight engine for deploying log anomaly detection models in a streaming context

rationale.text: She has experience with analyst-facing triage presentation, relevant to explaining alerts to plant managers.

sources.quote: A user-facing triage interface ranks suspicious chains by graph anomaly score.

rationale.text: Her stated preference for industry partnerships with real operational log datasets under NDA matches ArmaturaSec's traffic archives.

sources.quote: prefers industry partnerships that include access to real operational log datasets, even under NDA

constraints.text: The detector must work without labelled malicious traffic, so the design cannot rely on supervised classifiers trained on attack examples.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us

constraints.text: It must learn a site-specific normal baseline, raise flags on drift, and be explainable to a plant manager in plain language.

sources.quote: learns what normal looks like on a specific site and raises a flag when behaviour drifts from that baseline
explain to a plant manager in plain language

constraints.text: ArmaturaSec can provide traffic archives and firmware code only under NDA and can assign one to two engineers part-time.

sources.quote: one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our traffic archives

constraints.text: The target is Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP protocol traffic on embedded Linux appliances, with a dedicated security processor planned for the fifth hardware variant so inference does not affect packet forwarding latency.

sources.quote: Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP protocol parsing
dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency

constraints.text: Researcher capacity is limited for new large commitments until mid-2026.

sources.quote: has limited capacity for new large commitments until mid-2026

risks: Transfer gap: the researcher's published evidence is on logs, traces and PLC diagnostic logs, not on Modbus TCP/BACnet/IP packet captures; protocol-level anomaly detection must be tested in the first experiment.
No confirmed malicious traffic means evaluation cannot rely on supervised attack labels; success criteria using expert review, known incidents or controlled injections must be agreed.
A prior supervised classifier produced too many false positives; the new method could still generate alert volumes that clients switch off.
On-device inference and packet-forwarding latency constraints may rule out heavier models, and some cited methods use GPU/Kafka infrastructure not present in the appliance.
Explainability to plant managers is a hard requirement and may constrain model choice.
Researcher availability is unknown and notes indicate limited capacity until mid-2026.
Data access under NDA and client consent may limit how much traffic can be shared or used for benchmarking.
ArmaturaSec has one engineer reading about anomaly detection for six months; limited ML engineering depth may slow iteration.
questions: What PCAP or flow-level data can be shared under NDA, and what normal-period metadata (topology, maintenance windows, firmware updates, seasonal schedules) accompanies it?
Are there any known incidents, maintenance reports or operator notes that can serve as weak validation signals even if no confirmed attack captures exist?
What are the exact deployment hardware, memory and latency limits for ProtoSense and the planned fifth hardware variant?
Which site and protocol (Modbus TCP or BACnet/IP) should be the first pilot, and what false-positive rate would clients tolerate?
How should alerts be explained to plant managers, and what output format would fit ProtoSense?
Can you confirm your availability and capacity for a joint project given three co-supervised PhD students and limited capacity until mid-2026?
What NDA/IP terms would apply to data, models and resulting code, and how would client consent be obtained?
What support can ArmaturaSec provide for data engineering and model integration, given one to two part-time engineers?
